**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination**
- **Member name:** Skyler Jennings
- **Member ID:** W298663271
- **Reference number:** POC-E84DB56372-39024
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-17
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Governing policy:** *Spinal decompression surgeries* (HealthPartners), https://www.healthpartners.com/ucm/groups/public/@hp/@public/@cc/documents/documents/entry_256055.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back decompression surgery (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, of orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-17 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking HealthPartners to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file meet the criteria set out in the plan's own policy, *Spinal decompression surgeries*, including the imaging criterion the denial appears to rest on.

I have set the plan's published criteria side by side with what my medical records show.

## 1. A condition causing nerve root compression

The plan's policy states:

> "Clinical documentation indicates presence/diagnosis of a condition or conditions causing spinal cord and/or nerve root compression. The following list includes possible conditions and is not all-inclusive."

and lists:

> "A. Spinal stenosis B. Spondylolisthesis C. Spondylosis D. Spinal cyst E. Osteophytes F. Herniated disc"

My records establish this. My MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-25 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. That is both a herniated disc and spinal stenosis — two of the conditions the plan itself names — and the imaging describes the nerve root compression directly.

## 2. At least one sign or symptom limiting activities of daily living

The plan's policy states:

> "Clinical documentation indicates presence of at least one sign/symptom, associated with the condition(s), limiting activities of daily living. The following list includes possible signs/symptoms and is not all-inclusive."

and lists:

> "A. Radiculopathy B. Neurogenic claudication C. Myelopathy D. Upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain"

My records establish this. I have radicular pain going down into my right calf, and I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level seen on the MRI. My pain has been progressive for 14 months and is not relieved by rest. Not being able to stand for more than ten minutes affects nearly everything I do in an ordinary day.

## 3. Radiographic confirmation — the criterion the denial turns on

The plan's policy states:

> "Clinical documentation includes radiographic results (e.g., plain radiographs, advanced imaging studies), confirming the presence of spinal cord and/or nerve root compression caused by the condition(s) and supporting the indication for the decompression surgery"

My records establish this. The MRI of 2026-06-25 is an advanced imaging study. It identifies the condition (L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis), it confirms nerve root compression (compression of the traversing L5 nerve root), and it links that compression to the condition. My examination findings — positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level — match the imaging to the same nerve root and the same side as my symptoms. The imaging and the clinical picture point to one level, one side, and one nerve root. I respectfully ask the reviewer to look again at this study against the policy language above.

## 4. Persistence despite at least 8 weeks of intensive conservative treatment

The plan's policy states:

> "Clinical documentation shows the sign(s)/symptom(s), identified in criterion 2 above, persist despite completion of at least 8 weeks of intensive conservative treatments (such as exercise, medication use, or chiropractic care)."

My records establish this. I completed supervised physical therapy over 12 weeks, from 2026-03-28 to 2026-06-20. I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief. I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-30, which gave me about 2 weeks of partial relief and then wore off. My symptoms have persisted through all of it.

## 5. Conservative care within the current episode of care

The plan's policy states:

> "Documentation of conservative treatments must correspond to the current episode of care (within 6 months)."

My records establish this. My physical therapy ran from 2026-03-28 to 2026-06-20 and my injection was on 2026-04-30 — all within the six months before the request was reviewed and denied on 2026-08-17.

## 6. Physical therapy visits

The plan's policy states:

> "Conservative treatments must include physical therapy (PT), at least 4 visits over a course of 6 weeks or less, completed within the current episode of care (within the last six months, as noted above)."

My records establish this. I completed 20 supervised physical therapy visits over the 12-week course from 2026-03-28 to 2026-06-20, which is far more than four visits and is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. If HealthPartners reads this criterion to require some particular spacing of visits rather than a minimum number, I ask the plan to state that in writing so I can respond to it, because my records show a completed and documented course of therapy well beyond the minimum number of visits the policy names.

## 7. Active muscle conditioning and therapist's notes

The plan's policy states:

> "Active muscle conditioning is required as part of physical therapy. Physical therapist's notes must be submitted."

My records establish this. My physical therapy included core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work — active conditioning, not passive treatment — and it is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. If that discharge note or any other therapist's note is not in the file that was reviewed, please tell me and I will make sure it is provided.

The policy also addresses members who cannot complete therapy, stating "If a member is unable to complete physical therapy due to progressively worsening pain and disability, documentation in the physical therapist's notes demonstrating this is required," and "Note: The requirement for physical therapy will not be met if there is a failure to complete prescribed physical therapy for non-clinical reasons," and "There must be a physician's statement in the clinical documents that explains why physical therapy is contraindicated." None of these provisions applies to me. I did not fail to complete therapy and therapy was not contraindicated — I completed all 20 visits over the full 12 weeks.

## Request for the criteria that were applied

The denial notice says the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not tell me which criterion my imaging was found not to satisfy. I am requesting in writing that HealthPartners provide me with the exact clinical criteria used to deny this request, including the name and edition of any review guideline or vendor criteria set relied on, the specific criterion or criteria found unmet, and the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination. The plan holds these documents; I do not. I also note that the policy excerpts available to me describe their lists of conditions and of signs and symptoms as not all-inclusive, and there may be further policy provisions I have not seen. Please identify any additional criteria the plan applied so that I can respond to them directly.

## What I am asking for

I am asking HealthPartners to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-17 (reference number POC-E84DB56372-39024) and authorize the lower back decompression surgery, CPT 63030, requested by Dr. Duval. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice: my appeal must be received by **2027-02-13**, which is 180 days from the date of the notice. I am sending it to HealthPartners Appeals, MS 21104G, P.O. Box 1309, Minneapolis, MN 55440-1309, by [mail / email to DRT@healthpartners.com / fax to 952-883-9646, ATTN: Appeals], along with the completed HealthPartners complaint/appeal form and supporting records.

Please send your written decision to me at the address above. If anything further is needed from me or from Dr. Duval's office, please contact me and I will provide it promptly.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Skyler Jennings**
